cards.title: What is Federation?
body: Federation: (derived from a Latin word fidere, meaning,to trust) is a political system in which two or more states voluntarily from a union that leaves foreign affairs, defense, currency and foreign inter-state trade etc to the central (Federal) government, but retains powers of government over some internal matters. Indeed, the system Federation provides members of federal system will have equal standing or jurisdiction system.
1. Why was the Federation of Eritrea and Ethiopia not just and Fair?
2. Mention the defects of the Federation?
3. What was the task of Imperial Federal Council?
4. List the political parties represented the Eritrean Assembly in 1952?
5. Who was the first chief executive of the Eritrean Government in 1952?
Basically – Ethio- Eritrean Federation did not reflect the actual meaning of Federation; Eritrea forced to accept the Resolution 390 A(v) that federated it with Ethiopia without any alternative.

UNO, General Assembly passed a Resolution coded 390A (v) on Dec, 2, 1950 to Federation Eritrea with Ethiopia. At that time, USSR, Cuba, Guatemala, Checozslavakia, Norway and others opposed Federation Eritrea with Ethiopia, similarly USA and her allies supported and play a key role in Federating Eritrea with Ethiopia.

**Step 2:** The Federation between Eritrea and Ethiopia, established in 1952, was systematically weakened by Emperor Haile Selassie. On **November 14, 1962**, the Eritrean Assembly was forced to vote for the complete dissolution of the federation, and Eritrea was annexed as the 14th province of Ethiopia.

**Step 3:** So the answer is C) Nov. 1962.

cards.title: Model answer: defining a federation
cards.problem: (Short answer) Define federation and explain why the Eritrea–Ethiopia federation was not fair.

steps.text: Meaning: from Latin fidere, "to trust" – two or more states voluntarily form a union.
Division of powers: the central (federal) government handles foreign affairs, defence, currency and inter-state trade; members keep internal powers, with equal standing.
Problem 1: democratic Eritrea was imposed in a federation with autocratic, feudal Ethiopia.
Problem 2: Emperor Haile Selassie headed both the Ethiopian and the federal government, so there was no real federal government.

cards.answer: A federation is a voluntary union sharing powers between centre and members; the Eritrean one was unfair because it was imposed and the Ethiopian emperor controlled the federal government.

cards.title: THE FEDERAL ACT
body: The Federal Act consisted of seven sections (1-7) of resolutions of 390A(V) outlines the basic provisions were:
Eritrea to have autonomy (self- government) under the sovereignty of the Ethiopia crown.
The Federal government would have the power over defense, Foreign affairs, currency. Inter-state trade etc. And to levy tax to meet expense.
The Jurisdictions placed under Ethiopian government would have legislative, executive and judicial powers in domestic matters.

An Imperial Federal Council composed of equal number of Eritrean and Ethiopian representatives, would meet once a year. The council would provide advice concerning the common affairs of the federation as indicated in clause no3. Eritrean citizens would participate, in the judicial and executive branches and they would be represented by Ethiopia(Federal) government in legislative branch. Clause number 3.
The federation region would consist of one zone for customs purposes and there would not be any restrictions on the freedom movement of people and goods, coming into and out of the federal region.
The nationality would be same in the federation except for foreigners.
The federal Government as well as Eritrea would ensure the residents in Eritrea, without distinction/separation, of sex, race, language and Religion.

cards.title: Model answer: the Federal Act
cards.problem: (Exam question) Outline the main provisions of the Federal Act (Resolution 390A(V)).

steps.text: Autonomy: Eritrea would govern itself under the sovereignty of the Ethiopian crown, with its own legislative, executive and judicial powers in domestic matters.
Federal powers: defence, foreign affairs, currency and federal taxes.
Imperial Federal Council: equal Eritrean and Ethiopian members meeting once a year to advise on common affairs.
Common rules: one customs zone, free movement of people and goods, a common nationality, and equal rights without distinction of sex, race, language or religion.

cards.answer: Eritrea was to be an autonomous unit under the Ethiopian crown, with the federation controlling defence, foreign affairs, currency and taxes, and an equal Imperial Federal Council advising on common affairs.

lessons.title: Adoption of the federation by the Eritrean Assembly

cards.title: Adoption of the federation by the Eritrean Assembly
body: On December 14,1950,the UN General Assembly appointed the Bolivian diplomat Dr, Anzio Mateinzo to draft a constitution and organize the Eritrean government. He arrived in Asmara on February 9,1951.The draft of the constitution was then presented to the Eritrean Assembly. It should be noted that Ethiopia and Britain had seen to it that supporters of the union would have the upper hand in the Assembly.

Towards this end they had manipulated the elections in favor of parties opposed to independence. Consequently, in the 1952 elections the Unionist and the Moslem League of Western Lowlands (which supported the partition of Eritrea) secured favorable results. Those in the 68 member Assembly, the Unionist party gained 32seats,the Muslim League of Western Lowlands got 17 seats and the DemocraticFront19seats.The parties represented in the Assembly were:
Unionist party
The democratic Front
The Moslem League of Western lowland
The Liberal Progressive Unionist Party and Hizbi al Wetani.

The Democratic Front led by Ibrahim Sultan strongly opposed the moves to weaken the Eritrean autonomy. The Democratic Front demanded that Eritrean should have its own flag, Tigrigna and Arabic to be official languages.Moreover, they stated their opposition the placement of an Imperial Representative in Eritrea. Only the first two were accepted.
Finally the draft constitution was accepted with minor changes by the first Eritrean Assembly. The draft constitution included the following provisions:
The government was to be structured in legislative, executive and judicial branches
The Chief Executive to be appointed by the Assembly
Tigrigna and Arabic were to be the official languages of Eritrea
Eritrea was to have its own flag, seal and coat of arms
An Imperial Representative to be placed with mainly ceremonial roles and limited censorship
All persons were to enjoy fundamental rights and liberties.
The constitution and Federal Act were ratified by the Ethiopian Monarch in August and September 1952 respectively. TedlaBairu, the first chief executive and head of the first Eritrean Government.
Some of the weaknesses of the federation were:
Democratic Eritrea was federated with an autocratic and feudal(monarchic) Ethiopia through imposition
The head of the Ethiopian government and the Federal Government was Emperor Hailesellassie. Therefore, there was no difference between the Ethiopian government and the Federal Government.
The placement of the Imperial Representative that was not part of the Federal Act.
The absence of an article that invites for international intervention in case of violation by one of the parties.

cards.title: Model answer: the Eritrean constitution of 1952
cards.problem: (Exam question) Describe how the Eritrean constitution was adopted and its main provisions.

steps.text: Drafting: UN Commissioner Anze Matienzo (Bolivia) drafted it after arriving in February 1951.
Assembly: the 1952 elections, manipulated by Ethiopia and Britain, gave the Unionists 32 of 68 seats; the Democratic Front (Ibrahim Sultan) defended autonomy.

Provisions: legislative, executive and judicial branches; a Chief Executive chosen by the Assembly; Tigrinya and Arabic official; an Eritrean flag, seal and coat of arms; a mainly ceremonial Imperial Representative; fundamental rights.

cards.answer: Drafted by Matienzo and accepted by an Assembly dominated by Unionists, the constitution gave Eritrea its own government, languages, flag and rights, with Tedla Bairu as first Chief Executive.

cards.title: FOCUS QUESTIONS
body: 1. What was the task of Matienzo in Eritrea in 1950?
2. Explain the phases for the dismantlement of the Federation?
3. What do you think that the causes for the student‟s strike and worker‟s demonstration?
4. Who replaced Tedla Bairuin1955 ?

The Federal Act was implemented on September15, 1952. As soon as the federation started, Emperor Haileselasse began a systematic violation of the constitution and dismantling of the Eritrean autonomy, because his ambition was to incorporate Eritrea as an integral part of his empire.Ethiopian foreign Minister Aklilu Habteweld complained to Anzio Mateinzo the UN Commissioner that;

Thus, Ethiopia considered Federation as only a step towards union even before, the British Adminstration transferred the state property and key sectors of the economy such as ports, railways, cable and road transport, postal and telephone services as well as salt processing plants to the Ethiopian Government.
Thus, he started to erode the federation in three consecutive phases.

cards.title: Model answer: why Ethiopia dismantled the federation
cards.problem: (Short answer) Why did Ethiopia begin dismantling the federation as soon as it started?

steps.text: Start: the Federal Act took effect on 15 September 1952.
Aim: Emperor Haile Selassie wanted to incorporate Eritrea as an integral part of his empire.
Evidence: Foreign Minister Aklilu Habtewold complained to UN Commissioner Matienzo, showing Ethiopia saw federation only as a step towards union.
Method: a systematic violation of the constitution in three phases (1952–55, 1955–58, 1958–60).

cards.answer: Haile Selassie saw federation only as a step towards annexation, so from 15 September 1952 he systematically violated Eritrea's constitution.

cards.title: First phase 1952-1955
body: The Ethiopian government took the following measures to dismantle the federation:

It started to weaken the Eritrean economy by discouraging foreign investors and businessmen from involvement in Eritrea. It also closed some factories like SEDAO for hydro- electric power in Western Eritrea and FIAT-car industry in Dekemhare and textile industry.Others also moved them to Ethiopia.
Ethiopia banned formation of workers union but, BMA allowed for its formation in January 1952. President was Woldeab Woldemariam and deputy was Siraj Abdu.
The mouthpiece of workers union was voice of Eritrea (DehaiEritrea) Newspaper and its editor was Mohammed Salih. In 1954 the newspaper was closed and its editor was arrested.
Ethiopia and the unionists started to attack the Eritrean Labor Union and attempted to kill its president Woldeab Woldemariam.
The Imperial Federal Council was virtually dissolved in 1953.
Involvement in the appointment of ministers.

The first chief Executive of the Eritrea Government, Tedla Bairu and the president of the Assembly, Ali Mussa Redai were deposed by Emperor Hailesellassiein1955 and replaced by Asfaha Weldemicael and Idris Mohammed Adem respectively.
The imperial Representative,Andargachew Messay’s interference in the domestic affairs of Eritrea.

**Step 2:** Tedla Bairu was elected as the first Chief Executive of Eritrea in 1952 after the establishment of the Federation with Ethiopia. He resigned in 1955 due to pressure from the Ethiopian Imperial government.

**Step 3:** So the answer is A) Tedla Bairu.

cards.title: Model answer: first phase of dismantling (1952–55)
cards.problem: (Exam question) Describe the first phase of Ethiopia's dismantling of the federation (1952–1955).

steps.text: Economy: Ethiopia discouraged foreign investors and closed or moved factories (SEDAO hydro-electric power, FIAT in Dekemhare, textiles).
Labour: the workers' union led by Woldeab Woldemariam was attacked; its newspaper Dehai Eritrea was closed in 1954 and its editor arrested; there was an attempt on Woldeab's life.
Institutions: the Imperial Federal Council was virtually dissolved in 1953; the Imperial Representative Andargachew Messai interfered.
Leaders: in 1955 Chief Executive Tedla Bairu and Assembly President Ali Mussa Redai were replaced by Asfaha Woldemikael and Idris Mohammed Adem.

cards.answer: Ethiopia weakened the economy, attacked the labour union and press, sidelined the Federal Council and replaced Eritrea's top leaders by 1955.

cards.title: Second phase 1955-1958
body: In November 1955 a new Ethiopian constitution that completely ignored special status of Eritrea was proclaimed. According to this constitution all the islands and the territorial waters of Eritrea were put under the sovereignty of the Ethiopian crown. Some of the measures taken under this period were:
The appointment of Asfaha Woldemichael who had been the vice-Imperial Representative as a Chief Executive.
Ethiopia appointed Tedla Uqbit as the head of Eritrean police in violation of the rights of the Eritrean Assembly.
All political parties except the Unionist party were banned and an undemocratic election by bribery and intimidation was held in1956.
Tigrigna and Arabic were banned as official languages of Eritrea and replaced by Amharic (1956).

AsfhaWeldemichael responded by imprisoning the organizers of the strike.Despite the government crackdown,however, students were continued in many parts of Eritrea.

cards.title: Workers’s Demonstration
body: Eritrean workers staged a demonstration demanding to be recognized as a free trade unionin1958.The office of Asfha Weldemicael, ,refused to concede the reguest.Consquently workers throughout Eritrea came out on strike; soon they were joined by the general public. The confrontation culminated in brutal suppression of the strike by the government. Shots were fired against defenseless civilians as result 9 peoples were killed and 534 were wounded. Organizers of the demonstration were jailed. The strike was called off only after the government threatened to deploy Ethiopian armed forces. Once the demonstration was over, the government disbanded the labor union.

cards.problem: (Short answer) Describe the workers' demonstration of 1958 and its results.

steps.text: Demand: recognition as a free trade union, refused by Asfaha Woldemikael's office.
Spread: workers across Eritrea went on strike and the public joined.
Suppression: troops fired on civilians – 9 killed, 534 wounded; organisers jailed; the strike ended only under threat of Ethiopian armed forces.
Result: the labour union was disbanded.

cards.answer: A general strike for trade-union rights in 1958 was crushed (9 killed, 534 wounded) and the union was disbanded.

cards.title: Third phase Dismantlement 1958-1960
body: The final measures taken for the dismantlement of federation were as follows:
The removal of the Eritrea flag (Dec. 1958).
The Eritrean constitution was replaced by a new labor code (Sep. 1959)
The introduction of Amharic as language of instruction.
Change of the names of Eritrea Government and chief Executive in to Eritrea Administration and chief Administrator (1960).
Putting of Eritrean schools under the ministry of Education of Ethiopia (1960)

General Abiye Abeba replaced Anargachew Messai as Imperial Representative in 1959. He and AsfahaWoldemichael as well as Keshi Demetros Ghebremariam, the head of the Unionist party and Vice-president of the Assembly speeded up the final dismantlement of the federation.

cards.title: Model answer: third phase and the end of federation
cards.problem: (Exam question) Describe the final phase of the dismantling of the federation (1958–1962).

steps.text: Symbols: the Eritrean flag was removed (December 1958).
Language and schools: Amharic made the language of instruction; schools placed under the Ethiopian Ministry of Education (1960).
Institutions: Eritrean Government and Chief Executive renamed Eritrean Administration and Chief Administrator (1960).
End: General Abiye Abebe, Asfaha Woldemikael and Keshi Dimetros speeded the process until the federation was dissolved in November 1962.

cards.answer: Removing the flag, imposing Amharic, renaming Eritrea's institutions and placing schools under Ethiopia prepared the formal end of the federation in November 1962.

cards.title: Formation of Eritrean Liberation Movement(ELM)
body: There was individual and mass opposition in response to Ethiopia‟s violation of the constitution and the Federal Act but was not succeded. This shows, at that time conducting arm struggle inside Eritrea was so difficult.

In the meantime the Eritrean Liberation Movement was founded by Eritrean refugees in port Sudan in November1958. Among the founding members were;Mohammed Seid Naud,Salih Ahmed Iyay, Mohammed el-Hassen,Tahir Fedab, Yassinel-Gede and others. It was clandestine movement.
The objectives of ELM was:
promoting national Unity, securing independence and to set up ademocratic government.
The E.L.M organized its members from all social groups in cells of seven. Hence, it was known as Mahber Shewatte in the highland region and Harakat Altahrir al Eritrea in the lowland.
Due to its secret nature of organization its members did not know each other except for the seven members in one cell.
Thus, there was no coordination and close linkage among the members and even with the leadership living abroad.
E.I.M had no plan of conducting armed struggle from the very beginning. It planned to overthrow the government structure. Armed struggle was only considered in case the coup d’état failed.

cards.title: Model answer: the Eritrean Liberation Movement
cards.problem: (Exam question) Describe the formation, organisation and aims of the ELM.

steps.text: Founding: by Eritrean refugees in Port Sudan in November 1958 (Mohammed Said Nawd, Salih Ahmed Iyay and others), as peaceful opposition inside Eritrea had failed.
Aims: national unity, independence and a democratic government.
Organisation: secret cells of seven (Mahber Shewatte / Harakat); members knew only their own cell.
Method: it planned a coup d'etat, not armed struggle – armed struggle only if the coup failed.

cards.answer: Founded in Port Sudan in 1958, the clandestine ELM organised in cells of seven to win independence by overthrowing the government structure rather than by armed struggle.

body: The members of E.L.M were disappointed by its delay to start the armed struggle. Finally, ELM leaders planned to conduct armed struggle and sent fifty fighters to Sahel. Even though ELM tried to approach ELF to coordinate their struggle, ELF did not accept it. **Step 1:** From the lesson: “Finally, the supreme council of E.L.F decided to take military action against ELM thus, ELF attacked the fighters of ELM at the Battle of Ella Tsaeda in 1965.”

**Step 2:** **Step 1:** Recall the conflict between the ELF (armed wing) and the ELM (political/clandestine wing).
**Step 2:** The ELF leadership insisted on being the sole armed force in Eritrea.
**Step 3:** In 1965, the ELF attacked the small armed unit of the ELM at the **Battle of Ella Tsaeda**, effectively ending the ELM's presence in the field.
**Result:** Ella Tsaeda.

**Step 3:** So the answer is E) Ella Tsaeda.

cards.title: Model answer: ELM–ELF hostilities
cards.problem: (Short answer) Why did hostility develop between the ELM and the ELF, and how did it end?

steps.text: Delay: ELM members were disappointed by its delay in starting armed struggle; some left for the ELF, which began fighting on 1 September 1961.
ELM move: its leaders later sent fifty fighters to Sahel.
Rejection: the ELF refused to coordinate with the ELM.
End: the ELF Supreme Council attacked the ELM fighters at Ella Tsaeda in 1965, ending the ELM as a political movement.

cards.answer: Competition after the ELF started the armed struggle and refused cooperation led to the ELF attack at Ella Tsaeda (1965), which ended the ELM.
